name: Agarwood (oud wood)

card.summary: A dark, resinous fragrant wood from wounded Aquilaria trees, distilled or burnt as oud to give a rich woody scent that people wear as part of their personal presentation.
card.note: Wild agarwood trade is regulated under CITES; high-grade material is expensive.

quick.overview:
Agarwood, also called oud, is a resin-impregnated heartwood that forms when Aquilaria trees are injured and infected by fungi. It is prized for a deep, woody, balsamic scent and is used in incense and Middle Eastern and niche perfumery.

It supports appearance indirectly: a signature scent is part of grooming and how a person is perceived. The research on agarwood is mostly chemistry and pharmacology of the wood, not studies of fragrance and attractiveness.
quick.how: People wear oud as perfume oil (attar) or in alcohol-based fragrances, and burn chips as incense. It is often layered with other notes such as amber or rose.
quick.risks: Fragrance ingredients can irritate skin or cause allergic reactions in some people, and strong scents may bother others. Wild agarwood is endangered and international trade in Aquilaria is regulated under CITES, so sourcing and authenticity vary.

lead: Agarwood, known as oud or oudh, is a fragrant resinous wood produced when Aquilaria trees are wounded and infected by fungi, which trigger the tree to form resin as a defence. [1][3] The wood is traded worldwide and used mainly for incense, perfume and traditional medicine. [1]

For looks and grooming, oud is a fragrance choice: people wear it as a signature scent. Scientific reviews describe its odour as coming largely from sesquiterpenoids and chromones. [3][4] Reviews focus on the chemistry and pharmacology of the wood; no published study listed here tests oud as a means of improving perceived attractiveness.

Overharvesting has depleted wild trees and made natural agarwood a rare, high-value commodity, driving artificial induction methods on plantations. [1][3] Grokipedia reports that all Aquilaria and Gyrinops species are covered by CITES. [2]

chain: Oud oil or fragrance applied to skin or clothes
Scent becomes part of personal presentation
angle.text: Oud is worn as a perfume note so that a person carries a distinctive, lasting scent. Its role in appearance is as part of grooming and presentation.

paras: Healthy Aquilaria heartwood is pale and has little scent; the dark, fragrant resin builds up after injury or fungal infection. [1] Reviews report that the chemistry of agarwood differs considerably from that of uninfected trees. [5]
More than 300 compounds have been isolated from agarwood and Aquilaria plants, including sesquiterpenes and phenethyl chromones. [3]

The characteristic odour is attributed to sesquiterpenoids and chromones, and the smoke from heated wood has its own key odorants. [4][6] Researchers are studying how the tree makes sesquiterpenes and how fungi stimulate their production. [7]
Agarwood has been used for incense and perfume across the Middle East, South and East Asia. [1][2] Natural supply is limited, and plantation induction methods aim to meet demand more sustainably. [1]

Laboratory and review literature reports anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity of agarwood compounds, and a 2024 review discusses potential in periodontitis; these are not studies of appearance. [8]
